analyst_view.overall: A Madeira derby between two sides near the bottom: Marítimo are 15th with 8 points from 10 games (9 scored, 21 conceded, one point from their last five) and Nacional 13th with 10 from 11. Mitchell van der Gaag's Marítimo played 120 minutes in the Taça on 21 November (0-0 with Chaves, through on penalties) and have Paulo Henrique doubtful, with Rafael Fernandes and Yellu Santiago expected to stay out; only Yellu Santiago is in the numbers. Nacional, under João Henriques since 25 October (two wins in three), still miss Ulisses and Léo Santos for a while, with Liziero and Filipe Soares closer to returning and Wesley Gasolina unlikely (A Bola); the numbers now count these absences and have cut Nacional's goals for them, so last view's small cut is dropped. About 10,000 are expected at the Barreiros, A Bola notes Nacional have not won there in the league for 14 years, and the numbers do not treat the game as a derby. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and now take Gasolina, Liziero and Léo Santos off Nacional's goals (about -22% between them), which is what my earlier -4% was for, so that cut goes. Marítimo's weak scoring (9 in 10) and a tense derby point down, but their own defensive doubts, Paulo Henrique and Rafael Fernandes, which the numbers don't list, point up, so I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners and already add a little for Marítimo's recent corner count (+2.6%) and take a little off Nacional's (-2.0%). Marítimo at home in front of a big crowd should push forward, but Nacional's absentees are mostly central players and nothing I found clearly moves corners, so I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, already taking 7.8% off because Nacional have been booked less than usual lately, and they do not treat this game as a derby. It is the Madeira derby, both clubs are near the relegation zone and about 10,000 are expected (Record), so I lean higher by 10% to about 4.8. No referee is named yet, so this does not rest on him.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots and already cut Nacional's side by 7.8% for their low recent shot count. Marítimo should have more of the ball at home, while Nacional under Henriques have won twice 1-0 and may sit deeper; these pull in both directions, so I stay at 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target, already adding 4.2% to Marítimo because Nacional have conceded plenty on target lately. Marítimo's finishing has been poor and Nacional are without some attacking options, but the numbers' ratings and missing list already reflect both, so I stay at 9.7.
